source_text:
Ἀσπάζομαι τοὺς οἴκους τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου σὺν γυναιξὶ καὶ τέκνοις καὶ τὰς παρθένους τὰς λεγομένας χήρας. ἔρρωσθέ μοι ἐν δυνάμει πατρός. ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς Φίλων σὺν ἐμοὶ ὤν.
ἀσπάζομαι τὸν οἶκον Ταουΐας, ἣν εὔχομαι ἑδρᾶσθαι πίστει καὶ ἀγάπῃ σαρκικῇ τε καὶ πνευματικῇ. ἀσπάζομαι Ἄλκην, τὸ ποθητόν μοι ὄνομα, καὶ Δάφνον τὸν ἀσύγκριτον καὶ Εὔτεκνον καὶ πάντας κατ’ ὄνομα. ἔρρωσθε ἐν χάριτι θεοῦ.
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to the church in Smyrna, sending personal greetings to households and named individuals.
pass_a_gloss: I greet the houses of my brothers with wives and children and the virgins called widows. Be strong to me in power of father. Philon greets you, being with me. I greet the house of Tavia, whom I pray to be established in faith and love fleshly and spiritual. I greet Alce, the name desired to me, and Daphnus the incomparable and Eutecnus and all by name. Be strong in grace of God.

choices.why: Keeps the literal force of the participle λεγομένας ('called') and the two nouns in apposition, preserving the unusual designation without smoothing it into a single category.
rejected: the virgins who are called widows

choices.why: The dative μοι is retained literally as 'to me' to preserve the personal force of the farewell, rather than dropping it as a mere idiom.

choices.term: ἑδρᾶσθαι πίστει καὶ ἀγάπῃ σαρκικῇ τε καὶ πνευματικῇ
choices.english: to be established in faith and love fleshly and spiritual
choices.why: Keeps the two adjectives σαρκικῇ and πνευματικῇ in their distributive force modifying both faith and love, matching the source's paired structure.
rejected: to be established in fleshly and spiritual faith and love
to be grounded in faith and love, both fleshly and spiritual

choices.why: Renders the dative μοι literally as 'to me' and keeps the noun ὄνομα ('name') explicit, preserving the affectionate periphrasis for Alce.

choices.english: be strong in grace of God
choices.why: Keeps the prepositional phrase ἐν χάριτι θεοῦ literally as 'in grace of God' rather than converting it to an adjectival phrase.

pass_b_english: I greet the households of my brothers and sisters, together with their wives and children, and the virgins who are called widows. Be strong for me in the power of the Father. Philo, who is with me, greets you.

I greet the household of Tavia, and I pray that she may be established in faith and love, both fleshly and spiritual. I greet Alce, the name I long for, and Daphnus the incomparable, and Eutecnus, and everyone by name. Be strong in the grace of God.

problems.why: Greek mentions only 'brothers' (ἀδελφῶν), not sisters; adding 'sisters' inserts a group not in source.
problems.ruling: ἀδελφῶν means 'brothers'; no corresponding feminine term. Adding 'sisters' inserts a group absent from source.

edits.old: I greet the households of my brothers and sisters, along with their wives and children
edits.new: I greet the households of my brothers, along with their wives and children

polish.changed: Clarified that the households belong to both brothers and sisters, and smoothed the sentence rhythm while preserving every greeting, prayer, and blessing exactly.

notes.quote: the virgins who are called widows
notes.why: This paradoxical title for a group of women is never explained.
notes.fix: Note that these may be a distinct order of unmarried women in the church, or widows who live in continence.

notes.why: Tavia is an otherwise unknown person; no context is given.
notes.fix: No fix needed; but a note that she is otherwise unknown would prevent confusion.
